q: In which of these reactions is the named molecule REDUCED?
options: Pyruvate accepting hydrogen from reduced NAD to form lactate
Triose phosphate giving up hydrogen to NAD+ in glycolysis
Reduced NAD donating its electrons to complex I of the ETC
Pyruvate losing both CO2 and hydrogen during the link reaction
explanation: Reduction = gain of hydrogen/electrons. When lactate forms, pyruvate accepts hydrogen from NADH and is reduced, while NADH is oxidised to NAD+. In the other reactions the named molecule loses hydrogen or electrons (is oxidised): triose phosphate in glycolysis, NADH at complex I, and pyruvate in oxidative decarboxylation.
